NO HEADER. Level 7 part 2 (follows scan0078 '7 : MARIO 4'). WATER LEVEL: the floor of strips 1-3 is a 1-tile water band, written as pits (rows 11-12 empty) along the whole width. Mushroom platforms (thick dotted caps standing on stems with a zigzag top, SMW-style) have their caps written as '#'. The STEMS ARE LEFT EMPTY: as solid columns they would wall off the route; in SMW they are background. Stem columns: s1 c10 (cap c8-12), c16 (cap c13-20), c19 (small cap c18-20); s2 c8 (cap c3-14), c19 (cap c16-22); s3 c3, c7, c13, c20, c29. Enemies: bullet-shaped flyers = 'q' (s2 r5 c0, c7, c12); winged turtle s1 r6c22 = 'q'; dome/mushroom walkers = 'e'; hook/fin creatures = 'g'; s3 r4c15 'e' = hat-wearing thrower (hammer/boomerang bro) on the big cap, with chevron projectiles drawn around it. Boxes: X-hatched and '//' boxes and bricks = 'X'; '?' and '!' boxes = '?'. s2 c3 = door (2 tall) standing on the cap. s2 cols 0-1 = pipe rising out of the water (rows 8-12). Hanging structures under the water band are written in row 12: s1 r12 c29-32 (two '//' blocks either side of a downward pipe, the bottom of an upside-down pyramid; its lip also pokes into the top of strip 2 above row 0); s3 r12 c1-5 (top of strip 4's wall and entry pipe). CLIPPED above strip tops: s1 - a winged hatched turtle standing on the top cap c13-20 (cap is row 0), and a triangle platform at c0-1. STRIP 4 is an enclosed bonus room drawn only on the left half of the page (cols 0-21; the rest of the page is blank, so the strip is 22 columns wide). Wall c1-3 and wall c21 run full height. The entry pipe hangs from the ceiling at c4-5 rows 0-1 (it comes down from strip 3's water at c4-5). Inside: three 3-wide brick rows at r7 (c5-7, c10-12, c14-16), coin pairs r3 c8-9 and c13-14, '+' r3c18 = box with an arch marked 'P' (P-switch), exit pipe c20 rows 9-10. NO GOAL or next-level box is drawn on this page. Level 7's exit box '8' is instead at the end of part 1 (scan0078 s4 r7c36), so this page may be a bonus/secret section reached from part 1, or the two pages' order is uncertain. PLAYABILITY: with water as pits, the jumps between platforms are often too far: s1 cap c8-12 (r6) to small cap c18-20 (r10) has a 5-tile gap; small cap to '=' c27-29 has a 6-tile gap; s1 cols 33-41 have nothing over the water (9+ tiles); the top cap s1 r0 can't be reached (6 rows above the next platform). If the designer makes the water swimmable these go away. Decor: hills behind every strip.

NO HEADER. Level 6 part 2 (follows scan0076 '6 : MARIO 4'). The level ends at s3 r7c8: a box marked '7' (the next level), written as 'G'. Their content, as text in the same alphabet, is: S1 r-5:'                       ############' / r-4:'                       ############' / r-3:'                       ############' / r-2:'          q            ############' / r-1:'                                   ' (the ceiling slab cols 23-34 hangs from the surface). Strips 1-2 were converted from the drawn outlines by flood-filling the regions between pen lines. Regions holding coins, bubbles, enemies and boxes are water; the regions between them are rock. Strip 3 was transcribed by hand. Jellyfish (dome with tentacles) = 'q' (swimming enemy). Columns of small circles are air bubbles (decoration, not in the grid): s1 c2 r0-4, c31-32 r3-5; s2 c12 r0-1, c4 r6-7, c11 r7-9, c24 r1-4, c30 r3-4, c22 r9-10; s3 c0-1 r6-10. STRIP 2 MAZE: there are three separate water areas. (A) Top-left, rows 0-3 cols 0-12, with the X box at the bottom of a channel: it is entered from strip 1's right edge at rows 0-2 and is a dead end. (B) Centre, cols 18-25 rows 0-5, with 3 coins: it opens only upward, into the clipped area, so it is a dead end in the grid. (C) The main lower channel, rows 5-10: it is entered from strip 1's right edge at rows 6-8 and leaves through the floor shaft at cols 11-14 or the right edge at rows 2-8. Floor shaft: s2 rows 11-12 cols 11-14 are open. Two parallel lines run from strip 2's floor down into strip 3, where the shaft is cols 11-14 with walls at col 10 (rows 0-2 and 7-12) and col 15. STRIP 3 is only drawn in pen on the left (cols 0-15); the rest of the page is blank apart from faint pencil trees, so the strip is 16 wide and col 15 is a closing wall. The page bottom cuts strip 3: no floor line is drawn, so rows 11-12 are assumed solid, but the shaft (cols 11-13) is left open because it continues past the page bottom. s3: col 0 rows 4-12 = left wall. Raised block cols 2-9 rows 10-12. The solid block cols 4-6 rows 4-5 has an UP-ARROW sign on a post above it (rows 2-3 col 5), so it may be meant as a rising elevator block. In the shaft, cols 11-12 rows 3-6 are two tall boxes: the left one is solid, the right one holds a column of 3 coins (col 12 rows 3-5) and was left open. Cols 13-14 rows 4-5 = a sideways pipe stub running to the right wall. Coins col 10 rows 3-5 are outside the shaft. PLAYABILITY: strip 3 is entered from strip 2's right edge only at rows 0-3, because s3's left wall fills rows 4-12; strip 2's right edge is open at rows 2-8, so only rows 2-3 line up. The shaft gives a second way down. Water areas A and B in strip 2 are dead ends (see above). Decor: none besides the bubbles; faint pencil sketches on the right of strip 3 are ignored.
